title.narrative: UNJHRO - institutionellt stöd till skydd av mänskliga rättigheter
UNJHRO - programme support to protect human rights

description.narrative:
Stödet till JHRO har två komponenter: "Civic Space Project" och "Senior Women Protection Adviser". Genom projekten finansieras upp till 70% av MR-kontorets verksamhet i DRK och Sidas stöd utgör därför i princip ett kärnstöd till landverksamheten.
Komponenten the Civic Space Project syftar till att skydda och utöka det demokratiska utrymmet och skapa nödvändiga förutsättningar för DRK att förstärka sin demokrati genom full respekt för mänskliga rättigheter som bas för fred och stabilitet i landet. Att utöka det demokratiska utrymmet möjliggör för rättvisa och transparanta val på olika nivåer vilket utökar befolkningens aktiva deltagande. Projektet ska skydda och främja mänskliga rättigheter genom att öka både kapaciteten och ägandeskapet för nationella institutioner och civilsamhällsorganisationer att övervaka och rapportera efterlevnaden av mänskliga rättigheter. Projektet syftar även till att öka ansvarsutkrävande för brott, bekämpa straffriheten och skydda vittnen, offer och aktivister så att de effektivt kan utöva sin roll.
Förutom att aktivt arbeta för att övervaka och rapportera om efterlevnaden av mänskliga rättigheter kommer JHRO utbilda och träna nationella institutioner, civilsamhällsorganisationer, aktivister och journalister. JHRO kommer att stötta nationella institutioner som National Human Rights Commission, parlamentets MR-kommission och departementet för mänskliga rättigheter i deras arbete genom riktad utbildning samt logistiskt stöd. Aktivister, offer och vittnen kommer att skyddas genom aktiviteter såsom identifiering av "early-warning," skapande av nätverk och tillhandahållande av psykosocialt stöd. Genom logistik- och tekniskt stöd till juridiska institutioner samt assistans och juridisk hjälp till offer och vittnen, främst kvinnor, kommer straffrihet bekämpas.
Projektet implementeras över hela landet med ett mobilt team som täcker de områden där JHRO eller OHCHR inte har egen närvaro. Främst och till att börja med på orter där JHRO inte längre har egen närvaro ska lokala aktörer gradvis ta över ansvaret för att skydda och främja efterlevnaden av de mänskliga rättigheterna och folkets deltagande i demokratiska val.
Komponenten SWPA Project ligger under mandatet för FN:s generalsekreterares särskilde sändebud för sexuellt våld i konflikt och syftar till att stärka FNs möjlighet att fördjupa kampen mot konfliktrelaterat sexuellt våld i DRK. Projektet fokuserar på stöd till rådgivarens övervakning och analys av konfliktrelaterat sexuellt våld genom att möjliggöra en nära kontakt med konfliktparterna och stärka rådgivarens arbete att utöva påtryckning för skydd av kvinnor och flickor, pojkar och män. SWPA är baserad i Kinshasa och har till sin hjälp fyra fältbaserade rådgivare. SWPA koordinerar arbetet av de fältbaserade rådgivarna samt MONUSCOs MARA (Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Arrangements) i deras roller att övervaka, analysera och rapportera om situationen angående sexuellt våld samt identifiera och hjälpa offer och vittnen. Rådgivaren ska utöva påtryckning för att polisens och arméns implementerar sina planer för att minska sexuellt våld bland de egna leden, ska stärka icke-statliga aktörers engagemang samt se till att arbetet för att minska konfliktrelaterat våld är integrerat på strategisk och operationell nivå hos alla relevanta aktörer i FN-missionen (polis, militär, civil).

The support to JHRO has two components: a Civic Space Project and a Senior Women's Protection Adviser. These projects will fund up to 70% of the JHRO country operations and will, thus, in principal constitute core support to the office.
The aim of the component the Civic Space Project is to contribute to protect and widen the democratic space and create the necessary conditions for DRC to consolidate the democracy through the full respect and effective exercise of all human rights as a base for stability and peace in the country. Widening the democratic space will enable fair and transparent elections at different levels which will increase the active participation of the people. The project will protect and promote human rights through increasing both the capacity and the ownership of national institutions and civil society organisations to monitor and report on the human rights situation. The project also aims to increase the accountability for perpetrators of HRV, fight impunity and protect witnesses, victims and activists so that they can effectively perform their role.
Apart from actively working to monitor and report human rights, the JHRO will also educate and train national institutions, civil society organisations, activists and journalists. JHRO will support national institutions such as the National Human Rights Commission, the Parliamentary Human Rights Commission and the department for human rights in their work through targeted education and logistical support. Activists, victims and witnesses will be protected through activities such as identification of early warning, creation of networks and providing psychosocial support. Impunity will be fought through logistical and technical support to judicial authorities as well as legal assistance to victims and witnesses, in principal to women.
The project will be implemented country wide with a mobile team covering the areas where JHRO or OHCHR are not present. Starting in locations where the JHRO is no longer present, the responsibility to protect and promote human rights and people's participation in democratic elections will gradually be handed over to local CSOs.
The SWPA component lies under the mandate of the UNSRSG on sexual violence in conflict and the aim of this component is to strengthen the UN's possibility to consolidate the fight against conflict-related sexual violence in DRC. The project will focus on supporting the Senior Women Protection Adviser ‘s deployment to reinforce the monitoring and analysis of conflict related sexual violence, further engage with parties to the conflict to more effectively prevent CRSV and advocate for the protection of women, girls, boys and men. The SWPA is based in Kinshasa and is coordinating four field-based Women Protection Advisors. The SWPA coordinates the work of the field-based advisors and the MONUSCO MARA (Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Arrangements) in their respective role to monitor, analyse and report the situation of conflict related sexual violence and to identify and support victims and witnesses. the SWPA shall perform advocacy for the full implementation of the national action plans of the police and military to decrease sexual violence internally, shall support the engagement of non-state actors, and shall ensure that CRSV considerations will continue to be mainstreamed throughout the responsibilities of relevant mission components (military, police and civilian) at strategic and operational level.

UNJHRO provided the following three final narrative reports in relation to the projects on the Civic Space and People Participation Human Rights Promotion and Protection in the DRC and the work of the Senior women protection advisor and WPA Unit. A third annual report on the overall work of UNJHRO 2021 was also presented. Many results of were also documented in the independent evaluation done on the project.
Below are some of the results documented in the reports:
In the framework of the support to civic space and people participation in human rights protection, the UNJHRO have strengthened the role and capacities of the National Human Rights Commission of the National Assembly (HRCNA), the Ministry of human rights (MofHR) and the Inter-Ministerial Human Rights Committee (IHRC) and other National Human Rights Mechanisms and Institutions. This has proven to lead to some strategic results in the forms of new laws, policies and practices to address, prevent and reduce human rights violations in the context of law enforcement and justice systems. The MoHR and the HRC at the National Assembly positively commented the impact of UNJHROs support in enhancing institutions visibility and in raising awareness and understanding among the population on its obligations and on Human rights in Kinshasa and in provincial antennas. For instance, UNJHRO has provide technical support to Human Rights Commission of the National Assembly on laws on persons with disabilities and indigenous peoples, with the aim to enhance the Commissions ability to influence the content of the draft laws discussed in Parliament with respect to IHRL norms and standards. The UNJHRO also shared material on the rights of indigenous peoples and the rights of persons with disabilities for a HRCNA mission, form 29 March to 10 April 2021, to four universities in Central Kongo and Kwilu with the participation of about 1,000 students and teachers.
UNJHRO has also helped prepare a draft provincial law establishing the provincial truth, justice and reconciliation commission was passed by the Kasais provincial assembly and promulgated by the acting Governor. On a national level there was an increased number conviction by the judiciary and or disciplinary measures taken by oversight mechanism in response to human rights violations including SGBV. This is linked to the efforts by UNJHRO on capacity building on investigations.
In 2021, the OHCHRs Technical Assistance (TA) team based in Kasai Central province supported the collection and preservation of evidence in Kinshasa, North Kivu and the Kasai region. This involved for instance 04 autopsies, 36 exhumations of bodies (which have been kept in the Kananga laboratory awaiting autopsy) and 189 forensic examinations of victims of sexual and gender-based violence. Additional support was provided for the building and operationalization of a forensic laboratory in Kananga.
Furthermore, UNJHRO Improved judicial procedures and holding of trials of strategic/ emblematic cases. This led to a total of 20 JITs were organized to investigate serious crimes relating to international humanitarian law. At least 13 suspected perpetrators were arrested including the leader of the armed group RM NDARUMANGA. UNJHRO also contributed to 35 mobile court during the period between 1 Jan. 2020 and 31 Oct. 2021.
In 2020, the UNJHRO recorded 317 convictions: 162 members of FARDC, 68 members of PNC et 87 members of armed groups were convicted for crimes against humanity, child recruitment. From 1st to 31 October 2021, a total of 187 convictions have been recorded: 100 members of FARDC, 31 members of PNC et 56 members of armed groups were convicted for crimes against humanity, child recruitment. UNJHRO also helped improving the legal framework of the justice system so that is more in compliance w. national (Constitution) and international human rights instruments ratified by DRC. From July 2020 to October 2021 the UNJHRO held 20 monthly meetings, mainly with the Auditorat General des FARDC (high level Military Prosecutor Office) for the follow up of some emblematic cases (Chebeya, Yumbi).
Examples of some results that relate to an increase in access to justice are the trial of armed group commander Ntabo Ntaberi Sheka on charges of crimes against humanity and war crimes which began in Goma in November 2018 and concluded by his sentencing to life in prison for war crimes including m slavery and recruitment of children on 23 November 2020 in Goma (North Kivu) by the Cour militaire opérationnelle, following a two-year trail. Also 142 (including LGBTI) cases of protection human rights defenders and journalists among whom 53 women in the provinces of South Kivu and Maniema benefited from advocacy by the UNJHRO until the final end of threats. 47 of the 142 cases mentioned above also received funds from the UNJHRO and / or partners for their relocation (as a protection measure) among which 11 women. 89 human rights defenders were supported and followed by the advocacy of the UNJHRO and other partners until the end of the threats.
Together with UNDP UNJHRO developed and helped implementing a national strategy of prosecution on international crimes. The UNJHRO supported the setting up of a civil society working group to advocate for an inclusive process of TJ. The working group was established in April 2021 with the support and technical assistance of the UNJHRO. The working group is composed of the main engaged actors on TJ which can play a key role to support the national process and serves as a forum for consultations between the Government and technical and financial partners, with the aim of harmonizing different approaches concerning transitional justice. The working group also aims at sensitizing and helping to build the capacity of the population and communities on TJ. This group has already engaged in public awareness raising and outreach activities on transitional justice, conducted advocacy with the Government, and held five sensitization activities in Ituri, North Kivu, Tanganyika, South Kivu and Tshopo provinces.
On 13 August 2021, the President of the DRC established a joint committee to discuss the national roadmap on transitional justice. This committee includes the ministries of HR and Justice, and civil society, with UNJHRO providing technical support. The joint committee aims to inter alia propose a comprehensive and holistic roadmap for steps on TJ. The next steps are expected to include the development of a reparations programme, vetting of security forces, preparing a memorial process as well as ensuring close linkages with the Governments programme of Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Reintegration and Stabilization (P-DDCRS). The MofHR has also indicated a desire to move forward with a programme of wide-ranging popular consultations for the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission. These developments mark a significant step forward in the development of a national transitional justice framework for the DRC. UNJHRO has contributed to this result.
Another encouraging development took place in Kasai Central province on 28 June 2021 when the provincial Assembly adopted a decree on the establishment of a Truth, Justice and Reconciliation Commission. UNJHRO is supporting the establishment and operationalization of this commission. A similar process is scheduled to take place in the Kasai and Tanganyika provinces also financed by the PBF and supported through UNJHRO.
UNJHRO has also provided technical support to HoHR in drafting reports to ESCR and CEDAW treaty bodies. Besides strengthening the capacities of human rights institutions in the DRC UNJHRO has also improved abilities of the HR Defenders and Protection Networks to support NHRI work in safeguarding human rights. This has been done through several capacity building sessions with local NGOs, HRDs and protection networks and citizens movements. Also, a HR network of journalists has been formed that can contribute to promotion HR and monitoring/reporting of HRV. Training was also provided on how journalists can better protect themselves started in conflict areas.
Since 2020, the UNJHRO also reactivated the PNC/FARDC Human rights committees in the province. In so doing UNJHRO have participated in the meetings of these committees to monitor human rights violations committed by the police/ FARDC. These are constructive dialogue frameworks allowing JHRO/local NGOs to influence the security and civil authorities to respond in matters of respect, protection and promotion of human rights.
UNJHRO has also been involved in strengthened joint early warning mechanisms leading to better assistance to victims and prevention of HRV. Besides organising capacity building of local NGOs, HRDs and protection networks and support to human right defenders networks at provincial level UNJHRO also collaborated with a wide network of partners on early warning mechanism-alerts. Such systems were set up with local NGOs and focal points in Kalehe, Salamabila, Shabunda and Idjwi.
In 2021, the UNJHRO provided mobile phones (to 1 FP for each 43 Protection Network). and airtime for a first two months (Nov. and Dec. 2021) to contribute to enhance early alerts, follow up, monitoring and reports of HRV, strengthening the collaborations/sharing of information in due time with the UNJHRO and partners in the field.
To ensure that human rights are considered in provincial development plans and that no one is left out, a workshop on ESC rights, the ABDH, social auditing and the terms of reference was organised from 14 to 16 September 2021 for members of the government, MPs and CSOs of the province of South Kivu, in Bukavu.
Within the framework of the support to the Senior women protection advisor and WPA Unit, the SWPA has provided advocacy around the protection of victims' rights and reparations, including free legal aid to victims of CRSV. Advocacy has been made to the GoDRC and the 2nd Vice President who has promised to put these two laws on reparations on the agenda of the Parliament.
UNJHRO has also provided concrete support to victims of CRSV. As example, through the WoSH project, and since November 2020, 392 victims received holistic assistance including medical, psychosocial and legal assistance and 33 victims were assisted through socio-economic reintegration.
The SWPA has also held and through her various advocacy meetings with the first Lady of the DR, the Special Advisor to the President on SVC and with lawyers/magistrates, bar association.
UNJHRO has also held several technical trainings with the FARDC Commission in charge of the action plan to combat sexual violence and the PNC, with the Military Magistrates and Unit Commanders in four conflict zones and the Judicial Police Officers and Unit Commanders in SK, NK, ITURI and Kisangani and Tanganyika (only PNC).
Meetings with the FARDC Commission and PNC Department of Prevention of Sexual Violence and Protection of Children were organized. The DPVSPE will be deployed to conflict zones to disseminate the PNC Plan, train PNC and collect more engagement acts.
UNJHRO was instrumental to the passing and launching of the Addendum to the 2013 Joint Communiqué between the GoDRC and the United Nations against Sexual Violence in Conflict. In October 2021 the roadmap was presented to the new VPM and Minister of Interior for its endorsement and presentation to the new Government.
The SWPA and WPAs supported the implementation of a three-year action plan (2020-2023) on sexual violence in conflict developed by the Office of the President through the Special Advisor on Youth, Gender and Violence against Women, members of the FARDC and PNC commissions and other actors. The national FARDC and PNC Action Plan are with the Vice Prime Minister /Minister of Interior for endorsement. He shall proceed with the designation of appointees for the Commissions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
